title: SELECT DISTINCT
description: Learn how to use the SELECT DISTINCT clause to return unique rows from a result set in SQL Server.

data.text: Sometimes you may want to get only distinct values in a specified column of a table. To achieve this, you can use the SELECT DISTINCT clause.

data.title: SELECT DISTINCT Syntax
data.content: Returns unique values from the specified column(s).

data.text: The query will return unique values from the column. In other words, it removes duplicate values from the column in the result set.

data.alt: SQL Server SELECT DISTINCT - distinct cities
SQL Server SELECT DISTINCT - duplicate cities

data.title: Retrieving Distinct Cities
data.content: Return only unique city values from the customers table.

data.text: If you use the DISTINCT clause with multiple columns, the query will evaluate the uniqueness based on the combination of values in all the specified columns. It returns only rows with unique combinations of the specified columns.

data.title: Distinct City and State Combinations
data.content: Return unique combinations of city and state.
data.code:
SELECT DISTINCT city, state
FROM sales.customers;

data.alt: SQL Server SELECT DISTINCT - multiple columns example
SQL Server SELECT DISTINCT - multiple columns example before

data.text: In this example, the statement uses the combination of values in both the city and state columns to evaluate duplicates.
When you apply the DISTINCT clause to a column that contains NULLs, it will keep only one NULL and eliminate the others. In other words, the DISTINCT clause treats all NULLs as the same value.

data.alt: SQL Server SELECT DISTINCT - null example

data.title: Distinct Phone Numbers
data.content: Return unique phone numbers, keeping only one NULL.

data.text: Both DISTINCT and GROUP BY reduce the number of returned rows in the result set by removing duplicates.

data.title: GROUP BY for Distinct Values
data.content: GROUP BY can return distinct values like DISTINCT.
data.code:
SELECT city, state, zip_code
FROM sales.customers
GROUP BY city, state, zip_code
ORDER BY city, state, zip_code;

data.text: The above query is equivalent to:

data.title: DISTINCT Equivalent
data.content: DISTINCT can achieve the same as GROUP BY without aggregates.
data.code:
SELECT DISTINCT city, state, zip_code
FROM sales.customers;

data.alt: SQL Server SELECT DISTINCT vs GROUP BY

data.title: Tip
data.text: Use the GROUP BY clause when you want to apply an aggregate function to one or more columns. Use DISTINCT when you simply want to remove duplicates.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use SELECT DISTINCT to retrieve distinct values from one or more columns.
With multiple columns, DISTINCT evaluates uniqueness based on the combination of all specified columns.
DISTINCT treats all NULL values as the same, keeping only one.
DISTINCT and GROUP BY both remove duplicates; use GROUP BY when you need aggregate functions.
